Subject: Papillon renewal — latency & economics deep-dive

Alex —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached are the raw usage exports and our latency snapshot for Q1. I ran an initial pass to call out the three things I think matter for the upcoming renewal: token mix (70% embeddings-heavy), median latency during peak windows (~420ms on hosted r/w), and the recent uptick in long-tail generation requests.

Quick summary:
- Tokens: 1.9B total tokens in Q1 (list attached).
- Cost drivers: 62% of spend is from embedding batch jobs run at night; interactive chat traffic is smaller but latency-sensitive.
- Reliability: 99.86% success rate, but the 95th percentile latency slips during morning batch ramp.

Proposed asks:
1) Confirm whether Papillon plans to increase nightly batch size or move any of it to a dedicated pool.
2) If committed capacity is interesting, we can model a 12-month reserved plan that targets a 20% unit-cost reduction + 25% burst credit capacity.
3) Would you be available for a 30-minute walk-through Wednesday or Thursday so we can present option scenarios and SLO tradeoffs?

Next steps: I attached PAPILLON_Q1_USAGE.CSV, PAPILLON_LATENCY_REPORT_Q1.PDF and a blank mutual action plan. If you prefer, we can build three term options (pivot to dedicated, commit+burst, or keep hosted with ops credits).

Best,

All — attaching a concise commercial packet for the call (slide deck + three term tables). Key bullets:
- Option A (12-mo dedicated): list price $145k/month, effective unit -20% vs current, includes 15% burst credit and priority routing SLA (99.9% latency guard rails).
- Option B (9-mo commit + burst): $118k/month, -14% unit cost, 30% burst credit for scheduled windows; procurement-friendly signed SOW template included.
- Option C (hosted + ops credits): $95k/month nominal spend target, ops credits equivalent to ~8% savings and a best-effort morning ramp priority.

My recommendation: present Option B as the favorable path — short enough term to avoid long procurement timelines but provides meaningful cost relief and burst capacity for June growth. I also included a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration/testing cost ($10k).
